rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate all six compounds and identify critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A midrange temperature leaves room to tune selectivity in either direction.

Shorten the gradient another grid step to seek a faster fully resolved method while retaining the maximum CRF. The first pair is limiting, but its current resolution of 2.46 leaves room for further compression.

The 4-minute gradient retains the maximum CRF, but the first pair has little resolution margin. Raise temperature one step to test whether retention can be shortened without sacrificing that pair, keeping injection 3 as the fully resolved fallback.

Heating reduced the critical first-pair resolution, so test the shortest gradient at the lowest temperature to counteract compression through improved selectivity. Injection 3 remains the fastest confirmed method with maximum CRF.

Narrow the solvent window to make the 2-minute gradient shallower and lift the limiting first pair toward baseline resolution. The final peak will likely elute during the hold, but this could still yield a faster maximum-CRF method than injection 3.

Raise the final organic fraction one step to accelerate the late hold-eluting peak. This tests whether the first pair retains R ≥ 1.5 at the boundary between the fully resolved 0.75 endpoint and the faster but underresolved 0.95 endpoint.

Raise the starting organic fraction to restore the shallower slope of injection 6 while retaining the stronger final solvent of injection 7. This may recover first-pair resolution and shorten late-peak retention simultaneously.

Test one higher starting organic fraction at the temperature that best separates the first pair. This probes whether a narrower window can shorten the method further before weak retention causes early-peak resolution to deteriorate.

Return to the fastest fully resolved solvent window and test the next temperature step to establish its upper operating boundary. The first pair may fall below 1.5; if so, injection 11 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-CRF method.

The temperature and starting-solvent boundaries are now bracketed around injection 11. Lower the final organic fraction one step to test a shallower, potentially more robust maximum-CRF method, accepting a small increase in late-peak retention.

Shift injection 14’s solvent window downward without changing its slope to move the first pair away from the weakly retained region and potentially improve its resolution margin. The last peak should remain comfortably below 10 minutes, preserving maximum CRF if all pairs stay resolved.
